key_insight: The paper shows that single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuits can be classically simulated in polynomial time, even at sizes previously used to claim quantum advantage.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the barrier to verifying and optimizing large quantum chemistry experiments, enabling faster classical benchmarking of hardware-oriented ansätze.
method: Derive a polynomial-time algorithm for evaluating the energy of any single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuit.
Avoid dependence on quantum hardware locality constraints, making the approach broadly applicable.
Use fast classical simulation to optimize the circuit and search for lower ground-state energies.
evidence_signal: The authors report reproducing the 77-qubit, 10,570-gate experiment from Sci. Adv. 11, 25 (2025) in under a minute on a laptop and achieving a lower energy than the experiment.
watch_item: The result is specific to single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuits, so deeper or structurally different ansätze may not admit the same efficient simulation.
paper_title: Efficient classical simulation of large-scale unitary cluster Jastrow circuits
